summary: Satoshi Kawano, a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology, earned a doctorate from the University of Tokyo. In 2000, Kawano held a professorship at Kogakkan University.

Specializing in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies, Satoshi Naiki earned a PhD from Kyoto University. Naiki served there as an assistant professor (attested 2016-2020).

Satya Narayan Goenka (1924-2013) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under U Ba Khin around 1955-1971, founded the Vipassana Research Institute in 1985, and taught students including Joseph Goldstein, Sharon Salzberg, and Stephen Batchelor.

Satya Swarup Misra (born 1935) is an Indologist and linguist. Misra served as Professor and Head of the Sanskrit Department at the University of Lucknow (attested 1958) and as Professor of Indology and Linguistics at Banaras Hindu University.

Satyavrat Shastri (1930-2021) was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Punjab, Banaras Hindu, and Punjabi universities. He served at the University of Delhi (1970-1995, 2013) and as Vice-Chancellor of Shri Jagannath Sanskrit Vishvavidyalaya (~1989-1991).

Satyendra Nath Bose (1894-1974) studied at Presidency University and the University College of Science, Technology & Agriculture. He taught at Calcutta (1916; 1945-1956) and Dhaka (1921-1945), later serving as Vice-chancellor of Visva-Bharati University (~1956-1958).

Saubhagya Pradhananga works in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. In 2018, Pradhananga was attested as Chief of the National Archives of Nepal and as an editorial board member of Documenta Nepalica.

Sayadaw U Sīlānanda (1927-2005) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under U Paññāvanta, Mahasi Sayadaw, and at University College, Colombo. He served as abbot at several monasteries and became Chancellor of International Theravāda Buddhist Missionary University in 1999.

Sayadaw U Thittila (1896-1997) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Sayadaw Ashin Adiccavamsa and at Visva-Bharati University. He worked as a librarian for The Buddhist Society and the Adyar Library, and lectured at Rangoon University (1952).
Sayaka Sonoda completed a PhD at Toyo University (attested 2015-2016), studying under doctoral supervisor Shinobu Yamaguchi and co-supervisor Shogo Watanabe.

Scott A. Mitchell, a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, completed a PhD at the Graduate Theological Union under Richard K. Payne (attested 2008). He served as a professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2015).
Scott Dalby is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD from Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam. Dalby served as a lecturer at Amsterdam University College (attested 2014).

Scott DeLancey (born 1949) specializes in linguistics and Tibetology. He studied under Yungdrung Manang and held academic posts at the University of Colorado (~1980-1982) and the University of Oregon (~1982).
Scott Hurley is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned a PhD from the University of Arizona by 2001, where he studied under Elizabeth Harrison.

Scott Pacey is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies who earned a doctorate from Australian National University (-2011). He held posts at ANU, Hebrew University of Jerusalem, and the University of Manchester (attested 2014).
Sean D. Gaffney works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD at SOAS University of London under Tadeusz Skorupski (attested 2003) and also held a post there (attested 1996).

Sebastian Nehrdich is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned an MA at the University of Hamburg, where he studied under Harunaga Isaacson among others, and also studied at Kyoto University as an exchange student.
Sebastian Pole works in Indology and related fields. He completed studies at the East West College of Herbalism, the London College of Oriental Medicine, and the College of Ayurveda.
See Mui Yian is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Hong Kong under the supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2010).

Seema Alavi (born 1961) is a historian and Indologist who earned a doctorate from the University of Cambridge. She taught at the University of Delhi, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and Jamia Millia Islamia, becoming professor of history at Ashoka University (~2020).
